correctness.rationale: The exact eleven triangular seed values each have \(26\) set bits. For \(1\le A<2^L\), the identity \(A(2^L-1)=(A-1)2^L+(2^L-A)\) proves weight \(L\) by complementation. For \(L\ge5\), the three-block identity gives weight \(L+1\) for \(9(2^L-1)^2\). The condition \(K\ge L+30\) separates the three quadratic-expansion blocks. For each \(0\le j\le10\) and \(t\ge13\), their summed weight is \(26+2L\) or \(27+2L\), exactly \(H=t(t+1)/2\). The parameter \(K\) is unbounded, producing infinitely many distinct indices. A checker verifies the finite seed and sample boundary parameters; the algebra proves the infinite claim.

value.rationale: Published work poses a progression-length problem and proves an infinite six-consecutive case. This theorem gives infinitely many eleven-consecutive-index blocks simultaneously for each triangular \(H\ge91\). The simultaneous prescribed-weight result and the all-t parameterization make the new finding a structural extension, not an arbitrary numerical window. It does not claim arbitrarily long progressions or the minimal eleven-block.
